findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects, synced this morning." followed by a list of only three `<li>` items (Beta Launch Plan, Holiday Campaign Assets, Partner Integration Pilot)
findings.fix: Either add the missing fourth project to the list or change the copy to "3 projects" / add a heading like "Recent projects" that clarifies the list is a subset.
findings.violation: The stated project count (4) doesn't match the number of projects actually listed (3), and there's no label indicating the list is partial (e.g. "recent" vs "all").

findings.evidence: Workspace overview lists "Beta Launch Plan", "Holiday Campaign Assets", "Partner Integration Pilot" as the known projects, but Project settings shows "Vendor Onboarding"
findings.fix: Use a project name that appears in the workspace overview list (or add "Vendor Onboarding" to that list) so the flow is traceable.
findings.violation: The project name shown in Project settings doesn't correspond to any project named in the workspace overview, so it's unclear which project the user navigated into.

findings.evidence: `<form><label ...><input ...><button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button></form>` with no `action` or `method` attribute
findings.fix: Either make Save a plain anchor/button consistent with the rest of the navigation (e.g. link back to `#workspace-overview` or show a confirmation state), or explicitly set `action`/`method` and document the intended behavior.
findings.violation: Submitting this form performs a default GET to the current URL with the field values as query parameters, causing a full page reload - unlike every other transition in the mockup, which uses lightweight `#id` anchor links. This also means Save gives no visible confirmation or next step.

findings.evidence: `aria-label="Duplicate project"` with empty element content and no icon
findings.fix: Add visible text or an icon (with accompanying visible or sr-only label) so the button's purpose is clear to all users, not just screen reader users.
findings.violation: Sighted users will see a blank, unlabeled button with no visible text or icon, even though it's described as "Duplicate project" to assistive tech only.
